# How a reply is read

Every message that arrives in a sending mailbox is classified. A reply from a person stops that lead's sequence at once. Positive replies wake the operator; negative ones are filed. The rules are keyword-based, and a model-based reader runs beside them in shadow, deciding nothing until it beats them on labelled replies and the operator promotes it.

| Class | A person? | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| `interested` | yes | positive |
| `wants_more_info` | yes | positive |
| `wants_pricing` | yes | positive |
| `wants_call` | yes | positive |
| `referral` | yes | — |
| `not_now` | yes | negative |
| `not_interested` | yes | negative |
| `objection` | yes | negative |
| `wrong_person` | yes | — |
| `out_of_office` | no | — |
| `unsubscribe` | yes | — |
| `complaint` | yes | — |
| `automated` | no | — |
| `bounce` | no | — |
| `unknown` | no | — |

Mail from ColdOps's own addresses -- sending mailboxes, warm-up partners, test inboxes, the operator -- is never attributed to a lead.
